turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Hey Sam. Good to hear your voice today. How are you feeling after that second round last week?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey Wren. Honestly, pretty bummed out. Vantlow Software sent a rejection email yesterday, right after my second interview with them.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Ah, I am really sorry, Sam. That stings after making it past two rounds. Do you want to vent about it, or would you rather dig into what happened?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A bit of both, maybe. It just makes me spiral a little, you know? I spent six years running a shop, and now I keep worrying that hiring teams look at my retail experience and think it just won't count toward real customer success roles.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That worry makes total sense when a rejection hits. But turning around an upset shopper is retention work, plain and simple. Did they give you any specific notes in the email, or was it the usual template?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Total copy-paste template. Just that they decided to move forward with candidates whose backgrounds aligned more closely with the position. Which of course made my head instantly jump to my store work being the problem.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Canned emails leave you guessing, and the brain always fills in the worst answer. Remember that wedding order story you told me, where you saved the whole day? How does that story feel when you say it out loud?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That story feels natural because I actually lived it and solved the problem. But when they asked about things like churn metrics and SaaS onboarding, I felt like an impostor stumbling through vocab words.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Translating the vocabulary takes practice, but the core muscle is identical. You saved accounts long before you heard the word churn. What if you asked a friend in tech to do a quick sanity check on how you frame that transition?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That is probably smart. My old college roommate works in software support, so maybe she'd let me bounce a couple of answers off her without me feeling so judged.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: She sounds like a great person to loop in. Talking to a friendly face takes some of the pressure off. How is the store treating you this week on top of everything else?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Exhausting, honestly. We had a late inventory count on Monday night, so I'm running on pure caffeine and trying to squeeze in applications before opening.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Carrying a full-time store schedule while hunting for a new career is heavy lifting. Please be gentle with yourself tonight. Can you take this evening completely off from job boards?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, I really think I need that. Some takeout, a bad movie, and no looking at job listings until tomorrow.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That sounds like the right call. Rest up tonight, and we can pick up with fresh eyes tomorrow. Ready to sign off for now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ready. Thanks for keeping me grounded, Wren. Talk to you soon.
